statement: Call a cell (a,b) open if 0 <= a < n, 0 <= b < n, and there is no i with 0 <= i < len(mines) such that mines[i][0] = a and mines[i][1] = b. Call plus(k,a,b) true if k >= 1, (a,b) is open, and for every d with 0 <= d < k the four cells (a-d,b), (a+d,b), (a,b-d), (a,b+d) are all open. The function returns a result r, and exactly one of the following holds: (1) r = 0 and for every k >= 1 and all integers a,b, plus(k,a,b) is false; or (2) r >= 1, there exist integers a,b with plus(r,a,b), and for every k > r and all integers a,b, plus(k,a,b) is false. Equivalently, r is the largest order of an axis-aligned plus sign of 1's in the n x n grid, or 0 if no such plus exists.
preconditions: n is an integer with 1 <= n <= 500; mines is a list of length len(mines) with 0 <= len(mines) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(mines), mines[i] is a list of length 2, mines[i][0] and mines[i][1] are integers with 0 <= mines[i][0] < n and 0 <= mines[i][1] < n, and all pairs (mines[i][0], mines[i][1]) are distinct. Lists and indices are 0-based. The provided examples include mines = [], so the empty list is admitted here; if the original problem's 1 <= mines.length constraint is imposed, restrict to len(mines) >= 1.

statement: The function returns a result r, and r = 0 if and only if for every row a and column b with 0 <= a < n and 0 <= b < n there exists i with 0 <= i < len(mines) such that mines[i][0] = a and mines[i][1] = b. In other words, r = 0 exactly when every cell of the n x n grid is mined, so no open cell exists.
